newsitem.title: TAIWAN: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - June 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Taiwan newspapers - June 13.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Taiwan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
CHINA TIMES - Taipei's chief negotiator Koo Chen-fu and counterpart Wang Daohan from rival Chinese mainland may meet in Hong Kong at ceremony marking Hong Kong's handover.
Government agencies to implement five-day work week every other week from 1998.
UNITED DAILY NEWS - United States to issue visas for Taiwan citizens in Taipei instead of Hong Kong after British colony's July 1 handover.
Washington expresses concern over Taiwan's planned Han Kwang military exercise.
LIBERTY TIMES - Nationalist, Democratic Progressive parties to seek breakthrough on deadlocked constitutional revisions.
National Police Administration chief Yao Kao-chiao says murder of Taoyuan magistrate Liu Pang-you soon may be solved.
COMMERCIAL TIMES - Taiwan mulls revising two-in-one tax merger; foreigners' tax burden may not be increased.
Officials hold closed-door meeting to discuss issues related to Hong Kong handover.
ECONOMIC DAILY NEWS - Securities brokerages can buy foreign stocks for their clients.
Finance Ministry sends officials to supervise two local credit unions.
